title: Profile your audience
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who exactly is in front of you?
A student said that profiling is identifying people by age, demographics and socioeconomics, to define who they are and what they stand for.

I said that profiling can be more specific, as detectives profile a person, going through a process of interviewing and learning the inputs. I said that a book on the behavior of deceivers is useful for business.
I said: you cannot have authority unless you profile the person.
A student said: start super broad, like a decision tree, then get more and more detailed, instead of starting with small details.
Another said the two things to analyze first are the audience and the goal you want to accomplish with them, such as a college crowd or a room of business owners.
I said that a very safe start is understanding the learning styles and personality traits, such as abstract and random against concrete and sequential.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your audience's age, interests and goals.
Write the goal you have for them.
Write the broad profile first, then add details.
Write whether they are abstract or concrete.
Write what you will ask to learn more.

check.q: What did I say you cannot have without profiling?
What did a student say to do first?
What did a student say to analyze first?

recap: Profile the audience: broad first, then detail.
